items.q: In acute kidney injury, creatinine takes how long to start rising?
items.exp: Disadvantage 1: 24–48 hrs to start rising in AKI. (Book p736)

items.q: Creatinine is dependent on all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: Dependent on muscle mass, race, age and sex; obesity causes no change in S.Cr as fat doesn't affect S.Cr. (Book p736)

items.q: Which of the following statements about creatinine determinants is TRUE as written in the book?
opts: Creatinine is lower in African Americans
Creatinine is higher in African Americans
Creatinine rises after 40 years of age
Creatinine is independent of muscle mass
items.exp: Determinants as written: muscle mass (↓ muscle mass → ↓ Cr), race (↓ in African Americans), age (↓ after 40 years d/t ↓ muscle mass) and sex (↓ in males). (Book p736)

items.q: Fill up: Creatinine falls after 40 years of age because of the decline in ______.
items.exp: Age (↓ after 40 years d/t ↓ in muscle mass). (Book p736)

items.q: Fill up: In obesity there is no change in S.Cr because ______ does not affect S.Cr.
items.exp: Obesity: no change in S.Cr as fat doesn't affect S.Cr. (Book p736)

items.q: Fill up: Cimetidine and trimethoprim raise serum creatinine by competing with Cr for tubular ______.
items.exp: They compete with Cr for tubular secretion → ↓ tubular secretion of Cr → ↑ serum Cr. (Book p736)

items.q: On the inverse-relationship graph, by the time S.Cr reaches 2 mg/dL the GFR has fallen to about:
items.exp: By the time S.Cr = 2, GFR falls to ~60 ml/min. (Book p736)

items.q: A patient's serum creatinine rises from 1.7 to 2.8 mg/dL. Per the book's inverse-relationship examples, this rise means the GFR has:
opts: Fallen insignificantly because the patient was already in ESRD
items.exp: ↑ in S.Cr from 1.7 to 2.8: GFR falls significantly (50 ml/min → 30 ml/min); the 5→20 example is the insignificant one (already ESRD). (Book p736)

items.q: Which of the following statements about the GFR–creatinine relationship is TRUE?
opts: An initial creatinine rise corresponds to a trivial GFR fall
By the time creatinine rises, GFR has already fallen significantly
Creatinine rises before any fall in GFR
items.exp: Inverse relationship: by the time Cr rises GFR falls significantly; the initial rise in Cr corresponds to a significant fall in GFR. (Book p736)
